passages.text: “Be careful not to perform your righteous acts before men to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about righteousness.
He said, “Be careful how you do good deeds.
Do not do your righteous acts in front of people just to be seen by them.
If you do good deeds only to be noticed by others, you will not receive a reward from your Father in heaven.
God, your Father, is in heaven.
He sees what you do.
He rewards those who do good for the right reasons.”
passages.original: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς εἰ δὲ μή¦γε μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ Πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: So when you give to the needy, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be honored by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
passages.sermon:
When you give to the needy, do not announce it with a trumpet.
Hypocrites announce their giving in the synagogues and on the streets.
They do this to be honored by other people.
I tell you the truth.
They have already received their reward.
passages.original: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches his disciples about giving to the needy.
He says, “When you give to the needy, keep it private.
Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
Give in secret.
Your Father is God in heaven.
God sees what you do in secret.
God will reward you.”
passages.original: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι

passages.text: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. For they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners to be seen by men. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
passages.sermon:
When you pray, do not act like the hypocrites.
Hypocrites love to pray while standing in the synagogues.
They also love to pray on the street corners.
They do this so that people will see them.
I tell you the truth.
They have already received their reward.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: But when you pray, go into your inner room, shut your door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches his disciples how to pray.
He says, “When you pray, go into your inner room.
Shut your door.
Pray to your Father.
Your Father is unseen.
Your Father sees what is done in secret.
Your Father will reward you.”
passages.original: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι

passages.text: And when you pray, do not babble on like pagans, for they think that by their many words they will be heard.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples about prayer.
He warned them about how to pray.
Do not pray like the pagans.
Pagans use many words when they pray.
Pagans think God will hear them because they use many words.
Do not babble when you pray.
passages.original: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται

passages.text: Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask Him.
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God knows what you need.
God knows this before you ask Him.
Do not be like the pagans.
The pagans think many words will help them.
You do not need to pray like them.
passages.original: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν

passages.text: So then, this is how you should pray: ‘Our Father in heaven, hallowed be Your name.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught His disciples how to pray.
He said, "Pray like this."
He said, "Our Father is in heaven."
He said, "Father, let Your name be holy."
He told them to honor God's name in prayer.
passages.original: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς Ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου

passages.text: Your kingdom come, Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
passages.sermon:
God is our Father in heaven.
God has a kingdom.
We ask God to bring His kingdom.
God has a will.
We ask God to do His will.
God’s will happens in heaven.
We ask God to do His will on earth, just as He does in heaven.
passages.original: Ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου Γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου Ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς

passages.text: Give us this day our daily bread.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches his disciples how to pray.
He tells them to speak to God as their Father in heaven.
He says, “Give us today our daily bread.”
He asks God to provide what we need for this day.
He asks for enough food for today.
passages.original: Τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον

passages.text: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
passages.sermon:
God is our Father in heaven.
We ask God to forgive us.
We have done wrong things.
We call these wrong things our debts.
We ask God to forgive our debts.
We have also forgiven people who owe us.
These people are our debtors.
We forgive our debtors.
We ask God to forgive us in the same way.
passages.original: Καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν Ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν

passages.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’
passages.sermon:
God is our Father in heaven.
We ask God to guide us.
We ask God not to let us enter temptation.
We ask God to protect us from the evil one.
We trust God to deliver us from evil.
passages.original: Καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν Ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ

passages.text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
passages.sermon: God is your Father in heaven.\r\nGod forgives people who forgive others.\r\nIf you forgive other people for their wrongs, God will forgive you for your wrongs.
passages.original: Ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος

passages.text: But if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours.
passages.sermon:
God is your heavenly Father.
God forgives sins.
People sometimes sin against you.
If you do not forgive people when they sin against you, God will not forgive your sins.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν οὐδὲ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν

passages.text: When you fast, do not be somber like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces to show men they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they already have their full reward.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about fasting.
When you fast, do not act sad like the hypocrites.
Hypocrites make their faces look gloomy.
They do this so people will see they are fasting.
I tell you the truth.
They have already received their reward.
passages.original: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν

passages.text: But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, so that your fasting will not be obvious to men, but only to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about fasting.
When you fast, take care of yourself.
Anoint your head.
Wash your face.
Do not let people see that you are fasting.
Let only your Father see.
Your Father is unseen.
Your Father sees what you do in secret.
Your Father will reward you.
passages.original: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ Πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ καὶ ὁ Πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι

passages.text: Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He warned them about earthly treasures.
Do not gather treasures for yourselves on earth.
Moths can destroy these treasures.
Rust can also destroy them.
Thieves can break in.
Thieves can steal these treasures.
passages.original: Μὴ θησαυρίζετε ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὅπου σὴς καὶ βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ ὅπου κλέπται διορύσσουσιν καὶ κλέπτουσιν

passages.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moth and rust do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to his disciples.
He teaches them about true wealth.
He says, “Store up treasures for yourselves in heaven.”
Heaven is a place where moths do not destroy treasures.
Rust does not ruin treasures in heaven.
Thieves do not break in or steal treasures in heaven.
Heavenly treasures are safe and lasting.
passages.original: θησαυρίζετε δὲ ὑμῖν θησαυροὺς ἐν οὐρανῷ ὅπου οὔτε σὴς οὔτε βρῶσις ἀφανίζει καὶ ὅπου κλέπται οὐ διορύσσουσιν οὐδὲ κλέπτουσιν

passages.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches about treasures and the heart.
Your treasure is what you value most.
Your heart follows what you value.
Where you keep your treasure, your heart will be there too.
passages.original: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρός σου ἐκεῖ ἔσται καὶ ἡ καρδία σου

passages.text: The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking to his disciples.
The eye is the lamp of the body.
The eye lets light into the body.
If your eyes are good, your whole body will be full of light.
passages.original: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός ἐὰν οὖν ᾖ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται

passages.text: But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches about the eye and the body.
The eye is the lamp of the body.
If your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness.
If the light inside you is darkness, the darkness is very great.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται εἰ οὖν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ σκότος ἐστίν τὸ σκότος πόσον

passages.text: No one can serve two masters: Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.
passages.sermon:
No one can serve two masters.
A person will hate one master and love the other.
A person will be devoted to one master and despise the other.
You cannot serve both God and money.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ

passages.text: Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He said, "Do not worry about your life."
Do not worry about what you will eat.
Do not worry about what you will drink.
Do not worry about your body.
Do not worry about what you will wear.
Life is more important than food.
The body is more important than clothes.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν τί φάγητε ἢ τί πίητε μηδὲ τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν τί ἐνδύσησθε οὐχὶ ἡ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος

passages.text: Look at the birds of the air: They do not sow or reap or gather into barns—and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not much more valuable than they?
passages.sermon:
God is your heavenly Father.
God cares for you.
Look at the birds in the sky.
The birds do not plant seeds.
The birds do not harvest crops.
The birds do not store food in barns.
God feeds the birds.
You are much more valuable than the birds.
passages.original: ἐμβλέψατε εἰς τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν οὐδὲ συνάγουσιν εἰς ἀποθήκας καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος τρέφει αὐτά οὐχ ὑμεῖς μᾶλλον διαφέρετε αὐτῶν

passages.text: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them about worry.
He asked a question.
He said, “Can any one of you add even a single hour to your life by worrying?”
No one can make their life longer by worrying.
Worry does not give you more time.
passages.original: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται προσθεῖναι ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ πῆχυν ἕνα

passages.text: And why do you worry about clothes? Consider how the lilies of the field grow: They do not labor or spin.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about worry.
He asked, "Why do you worry about clothes?"
He told them to look at the lilies in the field.
The lilies grow.
The lilies do not work hard.
The lilies do not spin thread.
passages.original: Καὶ περὶ ἐνδύματος τί μεριμνᾶτε καταμάθετε τὰ κρίνα τοῦ ἀγροῦ πῶς αὐξάνουσιν οὐ κοπιῶσιν οὐδὲ νήθουσιν

passages.text: Yet I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said something important.
Solomon was a great king of Israel.
Solomon had much glory and wealth.
Solomon wore beautiful clothes.
But even Solomon was not dressed like one of these lilies.
God made the lilies of the field beautiful.
Not even Solomon, in all his glory, looked as beautiful as a lily.
passages.original: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων

passages.text: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe you, O you of little faith?
passages.sermon:
God cares for the grass of the field.
The grass lives today.
Tomorrow, people throw the grass into the furnace.
God clothes the grass beautifully.
You are more valuable than grass.
God will clothe you much more.
You have little faith.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τὸν χόρτον τοῦ ἀγροῦ σήμερον ὄντα καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ Θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέννυσιν οὐ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς ὀλιγόπιστοι

passages.text: Therefore do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them not to worry.
He said, “Do not worry about your needs.”
Do not say, “What shall we eat?”
Do not say, “What shall we drink?”
Do not say, “What shall we wear?”
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε λέγοντες Τί φάγωμεν ἤ Τί πίωμεν ἤ Τί περιβαλώμεθα

passages.text: For the Gentiles strive after all these things, and your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
passages.sermon: The Gentiles seek all these things.\r\nYour heavenly Father knows you need all these things.
passages.original: πάντα γὰρ ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνη ἐπιζητοῦσιν οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων

passages.text: But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all these things will be added unto you.
passages.sermon:
God is your heavenly Father.
God knows what you need.
Seek the kingdom of God first.
Seek God's righteousness first.
God will give you everything you need.
passages.original: ζητεῖτε δὲ πρῶτον τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῦτα πάντα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν

passages.text: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them about worry.
He said, “Do not worry about tomorrow.”
Tomorrow will take care of itself.
Each day has enough trouble of its own.
passages.original: Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς
